title: Patchcord workflow definition (schema_version 1)
description: Structural schema for a Patchcord workflow definition file (internal/workflow.Definition, vision document section 7.5). A future schema_version 2 gets its own schema file rather than a breaking change to this one (non-negotiable #5: public contracts are versioned). This schema checks shape only — it does not replace `patchcord workflow validate`, which additionally checks semantics no JSON Schema can express (e.g. that every `uses` names an action a given agent actually has installed, or that `else_of`/`if` reference real step ids).

id.description: The workflow's identifier. Stable across versions — versions of the same workflow share this id.

version.description: This definition's version. Published versions are immutable (ADR-0008) — bump this to publish a changed definition. `patchcord bundle dev`/`patchcord dev` auto-assign a version instead when this isn't bumped (ADR-0055).

steps.description: A workflow must declare at least one step.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression ("minute hour dom month dow"). Required when type is "schedule", rejected otherwise. See ADR-0035.

on_missed.description: Only meaningful when type is "schedule". Defaults to "skip" when omitted. See ADR-0035.

secret_ref.description: Checks an inbound webhook request's shared secret header. Required when type is "webhook", rejected otherwise. See ADR-0037.

name.description: Referenced by a step as ${{ workflow.inputs.<name> }}.

required.description: Rejected together with `default` — a default would silently satisfy `required`, making the flag meaningless.

default.description: Used when a run does not supply this input. Its type must match `type`.

enum.description: Required when type is "enum", rejected otherwise.

id.description: Referenced by later steps as steps.<id>.outputs.<key>.

uses.description: The action identifier this step invokes, e.g. "text.uppercase@1".

with.description: The action's input values. A string value that is entirely one ${{ ... }} expression is resolved against workflow inputs or a prior step's outputs; every other value is passed through unchanged.

connector.description: Must be entirely one ${{ ... }} expression — never a literal connector id, so a published workflow version never bakes in one deployment's connector identity. See ADR-0021.

if.description: A literal bool, or a ${{ ... }} expression that must resolve to one. A step whose `if` resolves to false is recorded as skipped. See ADR-0031.

foreach.description: A literal list, or a ${{ ... }} expression that must resolve to one. Runs this step once per item, with the current item available to `with` as ${{ each }}. Outputs become arrays. See ADR-0032.

stop_if_false.description: When `if` resolves to false, skips this step and every step after it, ending the run as succeeded instead of just skipping this one step. Ignored when `if` is absent. See ADR-0033.

else_of.description: Names an earlier step id: this step is skipped whenever that step actually ran. Chains build an if/elseif/else sequence without nesting. See ADR-0033.
